>
[Reaper's Grasp](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1184)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 165

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Arquebus](/Weapons.aspx?ID=195)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _[+2 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [arquebus](/Weapons.aspx?ID=518)_ has an ashwood stock plated with worked silver, featuring a mosaic of agonized skulls carved into the metal. The mere mention of Galt’s infamous [_final blades_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1094) is enough to make any mortal creature shudder. Used to execute political opponents in the nation’s constant civil war, these guillotines hold the souls of those they execute, preventing them from reaching a natural afterlife. When one of the final blades was destroyed in 4710, some of the metal from its remains made its way to Alkenstar and was reforged into a deadly firearm that retained the guillotine’s soul-stealing properties.

Whenever the _reaper’s grasp_ kills a sapient living or undead creature, a portion of that creature’s soul is drawn inexorably into the weapon, and another skull is added to the mosaic as if scrawled by an invisible hand, to a maximum of 10 souls. Creatures whose souls are protected by outside forces, such as a [lich’s](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3082) soul cage, are immune to this effect, though the process, while painful, does not prevent the soul from going to the afterlife or being resurrected. Keep track of the level of each creature whose souls are stored in the _reaper’s grasp_

**Activate—Soul Shot** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))   **Requirements** There's at least one soul stored in the _reaper's grasp_; **Effect** You channel the necromantic energy of a soul stored in the weapon into your next attack, increasing the attack's destructive power. Choose a soul stored in the weapon. The next Strike you make with the _reaper's grasp_ before the end of your turn deals an additional negative damage equal to twice the level of the creature whose soul you chose. Using this ability releases the chosen soul, and a skull on the mosaic fades away.

**Activate—Devour Captured** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))   **Requirements** There's at least one soul stored in the _reaper's grasp_; **Effect** You channel the necromantic energy of a soul stored in the weapon into a mantle around you, protecting you from harm. Choose a soul stored in the weapon. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to three times the level of the creature whose soul you chose, which last until the end of your next turn. Using this ability releases the chosen soul, and a skull on the mosaic fades away.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Reaper's Lancet](/Equipment.aspx?ID=810)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=126" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace](/Sources.aspx?ID=45) pg. 81

**Price** 200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Exquisite Sword Cane](/Weapons.aspx?ID=132)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Hendrid Pratchett himself designed this custom skull-topped _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [exquisite sword cane](/Weapons.aspx?ID=132)_ and had it gilded in high-quality gold. Its first victim was the very smith whom Pratchett commissioned to craft the weapon, so the means of its construction are a secret known only to Pratchett. The magic of the _Reaper's Lancet_ applies to both the blade and the sheath, making them each effectively a _+1 striking weapon_, but only if both are wielded by the same creature—if the two components are shared between creatures, only the blade retains the rune's magic. 

_Reaper's Lancet_ has a hidden reservoir inside the skull that automatically applies a new dose of poison to the blade after the previous dose was expended with a successful Strike. The reservoir must be filled manually (a process requiring 1 minute) and is large enough to hold only 3 doses at a time. Any sort of [injury](/Traits.aspx?ID=97)-delivered poison can be placed in it, though all doses must be of the same poison. The Price of the poison is not reflected in this weapon's listed Price.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact;   **Trigger** You damage a creature with _Reaper's Lancet_;  **Effect** You poison the creature you hit with the poison currently in the reservoir.

</column>

As long as you carry this weapon, your presence repels and noticeably unnerves most animals, causing them to avoid you if possible and react to you with a starting attitude one step worse than normal if made to interact with you directly. >
[Rebirth Potion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2090)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Potion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=130" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 90

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A small bit from a [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91)—such as a hair, scale, or feather—steeps in the clear liquid of a _rebirth potion_. When the potion is created, this bit determines the ancestry and heritage the potion changes the imbiber to. After you drink the potion, you transform into that ancestry over 8 hours during your next period of rest, finishing the transformation after the 8 hours are up. Throughout this time, you are [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), and [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37). Once the transformation is complete, the potion's magic ends and can't be [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371). Replace your ancestry Hit Points, size, Speeds, ability boosts, ability flaws, traits, and special abilities with those of your new ancestry. You lose your ancestry feats, selecting replacements valid for your new ancestry. You have mild control over the change, but you end up with a unique appearance fitting for your new ancestry, and some quirks of your body remain, such as relative age, general health, scars, and missing digits, limbs, or organs.

 Drinking a _rebirth potion_ of your current ancestry works normally, allowing you to rearrange some of the cited ancestry elements and change your appearance (provided you abide by the potion's limitations regarding health and age).

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

**Bulk** 2

---

This _+3 [greater resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [greater fortification](/Equipment.aspx?ID=285) [breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=10)_ absorbs impacts for later release. While wearing the armor, you gain resistance 5 to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage and resistance 10 to [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75) damage. Keep track of how much damage the armor prevents from enemy attacks, as the armor absorbs that damage. After 1 minute, the absorbed damage disperses harmlessly and resets to 0. Only damage caused by foes or hazards powers the armor, not damage you take from yourself, allies, or the environment.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;    **Requirements** Your armor has absorbed at least 30 damage; **Effect** The absorbed energy explodes from your armor in a pulse of force. Creatures in a 30-foot emanation take 10d6 force damage with a DC 43 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. On a failure, they're [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet away from you, and on a critical failure, they're pushed 20 feet away from you and fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). The armor's absorbed damage resets to 0.

On a failure, they’re also pushed 10 feet away from you; on a critical failure, they’re instead pushed 20 feet away from you and fall prone. The armor’s absorbed damage resets to 0.

This smooth metal bar is short enough to fit in one hand. It has several inset gemstone buttons on one end and a small lens on the other. Popular with law enforcement and blackmailers alike, recording rods allow users to capture and replay incriminating scenes and are often concealed and triggered covertly to avoid raising the subject's suspicion.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** When activated, the rod records anything it sees and hears for 1 minute. Its lens acts as both eye and ear with precise vision and imprecise hearing. This recorded sequence can then be played back as many times as desired, the sights and sounds communicated telepathically to the rod's holder. The rod's recording sequence can be triggered manually by a person holding it, or it can be programmed to begin recording automatically in response to a specified stimulus, such as nearby movement or a specific trigger word spoken in its vicinity. For _basic recording rods_, once activated, the rod records for 1 minute, after which it loses its recording ability but can replay that same scene over and over. Rarer and more expensive reusable versions of the _recording rod_ operate similarly, but the recording function can be enabled a second time by permanently erasing the memory currently stored on the rod. A _reusable recording rod_ lacks the [consumable](/Traits.aspx?ID=36) trait.

[Recovery Bladder](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1264)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 19

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L 8 if inflated
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Tattletail developed this tether-covered bladder to help divers in Anuli's Crater Lake recover heavy salvage or escape dangerous underwater beasts. Pulling the ripcord causes a small, pressurized air tank to instantly inflate the bladder to the size of a rowboat, forcing up to 16 Bulk of attached items or creatures to jet to the surface of the water at a rate of 60 feet per round. Pulling the ripcord, or removing or affixing something to one of the many tethers on the recovery bladder, takes an Interact action. A recovery bladder can only be used once, as the quick inflation permanently stretches the bladder, and only a few tinkerers have the skills and equipment to refill a pressurized air tank.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #206: Bring the House Down](/Sources.aspx?ID=247) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn backpack

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Red Hand’s Satchel_ is an [_alchemist’s haversack_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2305), with a main section containing an extradimensional space like that of a [_type IV spacious pouch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3032).

Once restored, the satchel gains the following activation.

**Activate—Instant Alchemy** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You name and then produce a common [alchemical item](/Rules.aspx?ID=2934) of any level up to level 20 from the satchel’s main compartment. This item has the [infused](/Traits.aspx?ID=797) trait and remains potent for 24 hours. Make a flat check with a DC equal to the alchemical item’s level. On failure, you can’t activate _Red Hand’s Satchel_ in this way until the next time you make your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575).

</column>

fields.text: Item 7 Red Thread Knot May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts Rare Invested Magical Source Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall pg. 74 Price 360 gp Usage worn This small length of red thread is knotted six times, with a loop at each end so it can either be worn as a bracelet or anklet, or hung from a strap. Activate Reaction envision; Trigger You critically fail a save; Effect The knot unties one of its six knots, altering your fate in the process. Treat your saving throw as if you failed the check rather than critically failed the check. This is a fortune effect. Once the sixth knot unties, it becomes a non-magical red thread.

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Composed to look like an important document, a _red-handed missive_ is a trap used by those who suspect someone has been going through their correspondence. If activated, the missive dissolves into red dye that coats anything touching the missive. Magic in the dye prevents it from washing off for 1 week.

</column>

>
[Red-Rib Gill Mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1447)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 76

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This mask is made from the gills of the red-rib salamander, an amphibious creature unique to Terwa Lake. Once activated, the mask intensifies the odors of gaseous toxins, allowing you to automatically detect toxic fumes within 30 feet and their approximate source (making the source [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) instead of [unnoticed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=41)). You can't wear other masks while you're wearing a _red-rib gill mask_.

 After Activating the mask, you also gain the listed item bonus to Fortitude saves against [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96) effects; this bonus is increased against the deadly volcanic gas known around Terwa Lake as Dead Man's Breath, and possibly against other similar volcanic gases at the GM's discretion.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Once activated, the mask intensifies the odors of gaseous toxins, allowing you to automatically detect toxic fumes within 30 feet and their approximate source (making the source [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) instead of [unnoticed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=41)). You can't wear other masks while you're wearing a _red-rib gill mask_.

 After Activating the mask, you also gain the listed item bonus to Fortitude saves against [inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96) effects; this bonus is increased against the deadly volcanic gas known around Terwa Lake as Dead Man's Breath, and possibly against other similar volcanic gases at the GM's discretion.

>
[Redsand Hourglass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1815)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Blood Lords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #186: Ghost King's Rage](/Sources.aspx?ID=189) pg. 78

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This platinum hourglass is filled with red sand, is decorated with imagery of roses and whippoorwills with tiny black onyx eyes, and has the ability to manipulate time. Once used by [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) herself, the _Redsand Hourglass_ was stolen from Pharasma's court a millennia ago. While the hourglass is in your possession, you're immune to the [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35), and [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) conditions.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76), [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You fail a saving throw;  **Effect** You flip the hourglass upside down then immediately right it again, rewinding time by a few moments. Reroll the saving throw with a +4 circumstance bonus. You must use the results of this new saving throw.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You flip the hourglass upside down, unhinging you from the flow of time. You become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=32) for 1 minute. You can use this extra action only to Step, Stride, or Sustain a Spell.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You flip the hourglass sideways, pausing time for everyone but yourself. You cast [_time stop_](/Spells.aspx?ID=339).

**Destruction** The _Redsand Hourglass_ is destroyed if it's used within the [Dimension of Time](/Planes.aspx?ID=21).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

This _+2 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [coral armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=20)_, often favored by allies of [merfolk](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=73) and aquatic [elves](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=2), is made of living coral carefully harvested from the ocean depths. Legends speak of a variety of similar coral armors with distinct powers, but surface-dwellers know of _reef heart_ as a magic armor that makes it easier for them to travel under the sea. _Reef heart_ enables you to breathe underwater and gives you a swim Speed equal to half your land Speed.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_coral eruption_](/Spells.aspx?ID=887). If you conjure the coral underwater, it ceases dealing damage after 1 minute, but its duration is unlimited. If the magical coral remains in place for 1 year, it becomes non-magical coral from which a reef might grow.

---

An acolyte accidentally left fulu paper outdoors overnight during a divine ceremony to [Tsukiyo](/Deities.aspx?ID=48) conducted only during a supermoon, creating the first _reflected moonlight fulu_. When you Activate this fulu, you reroll your saving throw against the triggering effect and take the better result. If this new roll is a critical success, the effect is reflected on its creator, who's treated as the effect's target, with any void damage converted to vitality damage. A reflected effect or spell affects only the original creator, even if it was an area spell or one that affects more than one creature.

This mirrored metal fragment is bolted or welded to the face of the affixed shield. [Reflecting Shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2825)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 234

**Price** 18,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Shield** [Buckler](/Shields.aspx?ID=17)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This high-grade silver buckler (Hardness 6, HP 24, BT 12) is polished to a mirrorlike sheen. The shield functions as a [spellguard shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=325) that can also reflect spells. 

**Activate—Reflect Spell** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You're targetd by a spell; **Requirements** The _reflecting shield is raised_; **Effect** You attempt to reflect the spell on its caster. The shield attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the spell, with a counteract rank of 9th and a counteract modifier of +30. If the spell is successfully counteracted, it's turned back on its caster. 

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include at least 2,750 gp of silver.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 38

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattoo

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This subtle pattern of complex dots, sunbursts, and lines is difficult to make out, as it's a near match for the wearer's skin tone. Serving as a barrier facing inward, this tattoo prevents ostentatious expressions of spells that are internal to you, making them easier to hide.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [metamagic](/Traits.aspx?ID=107)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell of 2nd level or lower that affects or targets only you, you can hide that you're casting it. This has the same effect as the [Conceal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=640) feat.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City](/Sources.aspx?ID=13) pg. 76

---

This [steel shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=3) contains a smoldering core of magma that never cools. Whenever the _reforging shield’s_ current Hit Points are below its Break Threshold, the shield recovers 5 Hit Points at the start of its wielder’s turn each round until it is no longer [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2). Each time a character [Repairs](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) the shield, the shield recovers double the number of Hit Points. The shield has Hardness 15, HP 120, and BT 60.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Reinforced Surcoat](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1429)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Adjustment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=380" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 104

**Price** 2 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** applied to medium or heavy armor

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This surcoat is made of thick fabric and light chain, designed to protect vital areas. When you are critically hit by an attack, you gain physical resistance equal to 2 + the value of the armor's potency rune against the attack's damage. If the armor is in the [chain](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=1) armor group and you have its armor specialization effect, you instead increase the physical resistance from the chain armor specialization by 2. This can't reduce the damage to less than the damage rolled for the hit before doubling for a critical hit. However, the reinforced surcoat increases the Speed penalty of your armor by 5 feet.

</column>

fields.text: Item 0 Reinforced Surcoat Uncommon Adjustment Source Grand Bazaar pg. 104 Price 2 gp Usage applied to medium or heavy armor Bulk L This surcoat is made of thick fabric and light chain, designed to protect vital areas. When you are critically hit by an attack, you gain physical resistance equal to 2 + the value of the armor's potency rune against the attack's damage. If the armor is in the chain armor group and you have its armor specialization effect, you instead increase the physical resistance from the chain armor specialization by 2. This can't reduce the damage to less than the damage rolled for the hit before doubling for a critical hit. However, the reinforced surcoat increases the Speed penalty of your armor by 5 feet.

You can later activate the trigger to detonate one or more of the attuned bombs as long as they’re within 60 feet. **Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 15 **Price** 700 gp --- Sharp metal jaws wind tightly into the pressure plate mechanism of this snare. When triggered, the jaws clamp shut and spin, damaging limbs in the process. The snare deals 10d8 piercing damage to the first creature to enter the square; that creature must attempt a DC 33 Reflex save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) until the end of its next turn.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage plus 2d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), and it becomes [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage plus 4d6 persistent bleed damage, and it becomes clumsy 2 for 1 minute.

This leather bandolier holds up to three magazines for repeating weapons in leather pockets that pop open with the quick flick of a thumb. >
[Water Purifier](/Equipment.aspx?ID=877)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 115

<row gap="medium">

</row>

**Access** Member of the Pathfinder Society.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This small tube of metal and glass has an opening at one end into which water can be poured, leading to a series of interconnected chambers filled with purifying agents contained between various perforated walls. The purifier attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) and other toxins present in water or any other liquid poured into it. Alchemically-treated replacement filters can be purchased to more effectively filter out more dangerous substances, using the filter's listed level as the counteract level. The counteract modifier is +5 for the level 1 filter, +9 for the level 5 filter, and +17 for the level 10 filter. If you pour a liquid other than water, such as a potion or beverage, into the purifier, the filtration process negates the liquid's effects and ruins the taste. The center of the tube can be unscrewed from the ends to access and replace the chambers of purifying agents. Each filter can be used to cleanse up to 10 gallons of water at a rate of about 1 gallon every 20 minutes.

fields.text: Item 0+ Water Purifier Uncommon Source PFS Guide pg. 115 Access Member of the Pathfinder Society. This small tube of metal and glass has an opening at one end into which water can be poured, leading to a series of interconnected chambers filled with purifying agents contained between various perforated walls. The purifier attempts to counteract poisons and other toxins present in water or any other liquid poured into it. Alchemically-treated replacement filters can be purchased to more effectively filter out more dangerous substances, using the filter's listed level as the counteract level. The counteract modifier is +5 for the level 1 filter, +9 for the level 5 filter, and +17 for the level 10 filter. If you pour a liquid other than water, such as a potion or beverage, into the purifier, the filtration process negates the liquid's effects and ruins the taste. The center of the tube can be unscrewed from the ends to access and replace the chambers of purifying agents. Each filter can be used to cleanse up to 10 gallons of water at a rate of about 1 gallon every 20 minutes. This clear, tasteless tar causes the victim to emit waves of harmful mental energy that repel other creatures. Desperate users might consume this poison to keep enemies at bay despite the poison's debilitating effects. While you're [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) from this poison, a creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of you or approaches within 10 feet of you must attempt a DC 35 Will saving throw. On a failure, the creature can't voluntarily move closer to you; this is a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effect. Once the approaching creature has attempted to save, it uses the same result for all saves from that dose of _repulsion resin_.

**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of [_repulsion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=254).

<title

    right="Item 0+"

>
[Researcher](/Equipment.aspx?ID=880)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 116

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

In cities all around the world you can find temples, city archives, and organizations like the Pathfinder Society where scholars and librarians can be hired to do research for you or aid you in your own research. Each researcher specializes in a particular subject such as flora native to the Mwangi Expanse, leaders of the First Mendevian Crusade, or Absalom shipping routes. If you plan to hire a researcher, you must hire one for the appropriate subject. The GM can decide that an appropriate researcher is unavailable in a given location, requiring you to look elsewhere for a researcher.

 A researcher can be hired to do independent research or as a research assistant. Regardless of what they're hired for, you must specify the level of researcher you're hiring, which is typically not higher than the level of the settlement in which they are hired. When contracting independent research, you hire the researcher to study a subject on your behalf and report the findings to you upon completion. An independent researcher can provide information on subjects up to their level +4, though more difficult tasks take much longer to research. Once the research is done, the researcher presents the relevant findings for the subject as determined by the GM, which is typically the critical success of [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). The level of the subject determines how long the independent research takes. A researcher can provide information on a subject of their level after 1 week. The researcher needs an additional week for every additional level of the subject above their own. For example, a level 6 independent researcher can provide pertinent information on subjects of up to 10th level, but would need 5 weeks to do so. A researcher needs less time when researching subjects of a lower level. A subject 1 level lower requires 5 days, a subject 2 levels lower requires only 3 days, and a researcher only needs 1 day for a subject 3 levels lower. A subject 4 or more levels lower takes less than 1 day and typically not more than 12 hours, as the GM dictates.

 When hired as a research assistant, a researcher provides a bonus to checks during the [research subsystem](/Rules.aspx?ID=1205). The research assistant automatically [Aids](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) a single PC with a single skill check rolled as part of researching. If the research assistant is at least 4 levels higher than the level of the library, the Aid is a critical success instead, possibly granting a higher bonus based on the research assistant's proficiency. A research assistant can never help out with a library that's more than 4 levels higher than their own level.

 The GM ultimately decides if a researcher is available for a given subject. Particularly obscure subjects may be outside of the capabilities of a hired researcher and are best reserved as something that the PCs must research themselves. Pathfinders typically employ fellow Pathfinders for additional research and must do so by working with a local lodge.

---

In cities all around the world you can find temples, city archives, and organizations like the Pathfinder Society where scholars and librarians can be hired to do research for you or aid you in your own research. Each researcher specializes in a particular subject such as flora native to the Mwangi Expanse, leaders of the First Mendevian Crusade, or Absalom shipping routes. If you plan to hire a researcher, you must hire one for the appropriate subject. The GM can decide that an appropriate researcher is unavailable in a given location, requiring you to look elsewhere for a researcher.

 A researcher can be hired to do independent research or as a research assistant. Regardless of what they're hired for, you must specify the level of researcher you're hiring, which is typically not higher than the level of the settlement in which they are hired. When contracting independent research, you hire the researcher to study a subject on your behalf and report the findings to you upon completion. An independent researcher can provide information on subjects up to their level +4, though more difficult tasks take much longer to research. Once the research is done, the researcher presents the relevant findings for the subject as determined by the GM, which is typically the critical success of [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). The level of the subject determines how long the independent research takes. A researcher can provide information on a subject of their level after 1 week. The researcher needs an additional week for every additional level of the subject above their own. For example, a level 6 independent researcher can provide pertinent information on subjects of up to 10th level, but would need 5 weeks to do so. A researcher needs less time when researching subjects of a lower level. A subject 1 level lower requires 5 days, a subject 2 levels lower requires only 3 days, and a researcher only needs 1 day for a subject 3 levels lower. A subject 4 or more levels lower takes less than 1 day and typically not more than 12 hours, as the GM dictates.

 When hired as a research assistant, a researcher provides a bonus to checks during the [research subsystem](/Rules.aspx?ID=1205). The research assistant automatically [Aids](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) a single PC with a single skill check rolled as part of researching. If the research assistant is at least 4 levels higher than the level of the library, the Aid is a critical success instead, possibly granting a higher bonus based on the research assistant's proficiency. A research assistant can never help out with a library that's more than 4 levels higher than their own level.

 The GM ultimately decides if a researcher is available for a given subject. Particularly obscure subjects may be outside of the capabilities of a hired researcher and are best reserved as something that the PCs must research themselves. Pathfinders typically employ fellow Pathfinders for additional research and must do so by working with a local lodge.

>
[Resolute Mind Wrap](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3136)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 74

**Price** 360 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The followers of the Tan Sugi monastery understood the value of protecting the mind from the intrusion of violence and anger and infused this strip of striped green and brown cloth with their beliefs. Wrapped around the head, the stripes almost evoke the patterns of sugi branches coiled around the wearer's skull. The _resolute mind wrap_ grants you resistance 5 against mental damage. .

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You attempt a Will saving throw against a mental effect;  **Effect** The _resolute mind wrap clings_ more tightly to your head, granting you a +1 item bonus to your Will saving throw. If you succeed at this saving throw, the resistance to mental damage granted by the resolute mind wrap increases to 10 for 1 minute.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Resonant Guitar](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2616)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
<trait label="Sonic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=147" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 146

**Price** 1,850 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Every part of this dark, shining guitar, from the strings to the soundboard, is constructed of metal. When the strings are strummed, the gilding on the guitar ripples like a liquid. A _resonant guitar_ is a [virtuoso handheld musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37) that grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks attempted while using it.

 A _resonant guitar_ is a planar key for [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) and similar magic to travel to the [Plane of Metal](/Planes.aspx?ID=24). When using it in this way, you can play a tune inspired by your destination to make it more likely to arrive where you intend to be, appearing 1d6×25 miles from your intended destination instead of 1d10×25 miles away.

**Activate—Strum of Thunder** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You play a magnetic tune, enchanting one metallic weapon within 60 feet of you. This item gains the [_thundering_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=306) rune for 1 hour.

**Activate—Chord of Protection** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature within 30 feet of you targets you or an ally with a melee attack;  **Effect** You strike a piercing chord, putting up an invisible sound barrier between the target and the attacker. The target gains a +2 status bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the Strike still hits, the barrier breaks, dealing 3d10 sonic damage to the attacker.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

The end of this ammunition is a metallic tuning fork with magical etchings. When an activated _resonating arrow_ hits its target, the tuning fork resonates with residual energy from the shot, transforming it into dangerous sound waves. This deals 5d10 sonic damage to the target and each creature within 10 feet of it with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) DC 28 Fortitude save.

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

---

These supple leather boots are studded with tiny crystals.

**Activate—Chiming Steps** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to half your Speed. The crystals ring out with pleasant-sounding chimes that reverberate painfully in the ears of others. Each creature that you pass adjacent to during your Stride takes 4d8 [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) damage (DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2247) Fortitude save); a creature takes this damage only once. A creature who critically fails the save is also [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) for 1 minute.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 128 **Usage** affixed to armor or a weapon --- This two-pronged fork of metal emits a constant low hum, vibrating slightly when touched. The spell attack roll of any spell cast by activating this item is +9, and the spell DC is 19.
  • **Armor** You gain resistance 2 to sonic damage and a +1 item bonus to saving throws against effects with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147) trait.
  • **Weapon** After you cast a sonic spell by activating the fork, the weapon reverberates with trapped sound waves. Your next Strike causes the target to be [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 1 round if it hits (or for 3 rounds on a critical hit). If you don't make a Strike by the end of your next turn, the sound waves dissipate with no effect.
**Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You cast [_bullhorn_](/Spells.aspx?ID=877). Resonating Fork **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 128 **Price** 140 gp --- **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_biting words_](/Spells.aspx?ID=868). Resonating Fork (Greater) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 128 **Price** 340 gp --- The resistance is 5 and the item bonus is +2 when affixed to armor, the deafened duration when affixed to a weapon is 3 rounds (1 minute on a critical success), the spell attack roll is +13, and the spell DC is 23. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast 2nd-rank _biting words_. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_noise blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1616). Resonating Fork (Major) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 128 **Price** 1,800 gp --- The resistance is 10 and the item bonus is +2 when affixed to armor, the deafened duration when affixed to a weapon is 1 minute (1 hour on a critical success), and the spell DC is 29. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast 4th-rank _noise blast_. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast [_painful vibrations_](/Spells.aspx?ID=964).

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Hellbreakers</spoilers>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #222: Hellbreakers](/Sources.aspx?ID=307) pg. 210

**Bulk** L

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

---

A _restful salve_ is a compound that can be applied to the skin to prevent undeath. If applied to a fresh corpse, the corpse doesn't decay, nor can it be transformed into an undead or otherwise controlled until the sun rises the next morning. If applied to a living creature, this salve lasts for only 1 hour due to the body's natural excretions. For that duration, the salve wards off effects that would cause undeath upon dying.

This fulu depicts the five-spoke wheel of [Qi Zhong](/Deities.aspx?ID=314), god of magic and medicine, and burns away slowly like incense. If you fall asleep with the fulu attached to you and during the fulu’s duration, you regain double the amount of Hit Points you usually gain from resting. You also gain a +2 status bonus to saves against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects that occur in your dreams, such as the _nightmare_ spell, for as long as you remain asleep.

You also gain a +2 status bonus to saves against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects that occur in your dreams, such as the [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=208) spell.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 188

**Price** 320 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This four-person tent provides several benefits for those who rest within. The climate inside the tent is comfortable and allows creatures inside it to withstand most hostile weather conditions, but incredible heat or cold, powerful storms, and winds of hurricane force or greater can still damage or destroy the tent. Mundane pests such as solitary ordinary insects avoid the tent, though swarms and giant insects can attack the tent as normal. Once you pitch the tent, only you can easily move it; any other creatures must succeed at a DC 20 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to do so. Finally, the tent automatically camouflages with its surroundings, requiring a [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519) creature to succeed at a DC 22 Perception check to notice it.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 78

**Price** 25 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact or 10 minutes (concentrate, Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Resurrection tea_ was named for its repugnant taste, said to be “strong enough to kill the living,” and its incredible medicinal properties “powerful enough to raise the dead.” The primary ingredients in this medicinal tea are ginseng and jujubes, enhanced with additional herbs, shaved deer antlers, sugi tree bark, and a variety of mushrooms stewed for several hours in a large pot to form a brown, pulpy, and viscous liquid. The bitterness and earthy taste make the tea rather unappetizing. The tea restores 2d8+5 Hit Points, and you reduce the DC of recovery checks by 1 for 8 hours.

---

[Tea Ceremony](/Traits.aspx?ID=738) The tea reduces the DC of recovery checks by 3.

</column>

May contain spoilers from Curtain Call **Source** [Pathfinder #206: Bring the House Down](/Sources.aspx?ID=247) pg. 83 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- _Retribution_ is a [_+3 greater striking_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [_keen_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2843) [_shifting_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2846) [_wounding_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2854) [_war razor_](/Weapons.aspx?ID=307). **Activate—Vengeful Strike** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** You make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with _Retribution_ against a target within 120 feet that you can see and who damaged you within the last minute, as if they were within reach. Once _Retribution_ is restored, it becomes a _+3 major striking keen shifting wounding war razor_ and gains the following additional activations. **Activate—Cruel Cut** ([curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566), [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** Choose a target within 120 feet who you can see. That target must attempt a DC 44 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target takes 3d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86).
**Failure** As success, but one of their eyes is damaged, rendering them [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65). The target also becomes [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 1. The dazzled and drained condition are permanent until removed by [_cleanse affliction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1467) or a similar effect.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but 6d6 persistent bleed damage and the target is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) instead of dazzled, and drained 2 instead of drained 1. If the target is ever reduced to 0 Hit Points or less while under this curse, they immediately die. **Activate** Reflect Curse; **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You are about to attempt a saving throw against a [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=566); **Effect** If you succeed or critically succeed against the curse, it is reflected back to its source and it does not affect you; the source must then attempt a saving throw against the curse.

---

The blade of this _+1 [greataxe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=21)_ bears a design of a human skull. Whenever a creature damages you with an attack, the skull changes its appearance to look like the face of that creature. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your next damage roll against that creature before the end of your next turn. Because the face reshapes each time you're damaged, you get the additional damage only if you attack the creature that damaged you most recently.

---

This belt is covered in small pouches that clasp with buttons of painstakingly carved stone. The belt is tied to an extradimensional space that can hold one item of 1 Bulk or less. Anyone holding the belt can sense its contents, but only those who've invested it can store or retrieve items. Many retrieval belts are found with an item already inside. 

**Activate—Store Item** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))   **Requirements** There is room for an item in the belt; **Effect** One item you're holding with a Bulk of 1 or less vanishes into the belt's extradimensional space. 

**Activate—Retrieve Item** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))   **Requirements** An item is stored in the belt and you have a free hand; **Effect** The item stored in the belt appears in your hand. Neither Store Item nor Retrieve Item can be activated again for 1 minute.

This belt is covered in small pouches that clasp with buttons of painstakingly carved stone. The belt is tied to an extradimensional space that can hold one item of 1 Bulk or less. Anyone holding the belt can sense its contents, but only those who've invested it can store or retrieve items. Many retrieval belts are found with an item already inside. 

**Activate—Store Item** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))   **Requirements** There is room for an item in the belt; **Effect** One item you're holding with a Bulk of 1 or less vanishes into the belt's extradimensional space. 

**Activate—Retrieve Item** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))   **Requirements** An item is stored in the belt and you have a free hand; **Effect** The item stored in the belt appears in your hand. Neither Store Item nor Retrieve Item can be activated again for 1 minute.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Retrieval Prism](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1032)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 176

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) A basic retrieval prism must be attuned to a PC to function._

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>command</row></row>

 

 

**Requirement** You have a free hand.
</row>

</column>

---

This triangular prism showing swirling black patterns inside constantly moves around on your armor, no matter where you affix it. As part of the process of Affixing this Talisman, you attune it to a single item of 1 Bulk or less. When you activate this talisman, the attuned item immediately teleports into your hand.

 The _retrieval prism_ can't retrieve an item that's not on your plane, including one that's in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) space like a [_bag of holding_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=249). If you haven't expended the talisman, you can attune it to a different item by Affixing the Talisman again.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Kept in an airtight spray bottle, revealing mist is an alchemical concoction that creates a sticky and clinging mist of chemicals in a 15-foot cone when sprayed. It doesn't affect visibility but causes [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) creatures in the area to be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) rather than [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39). Revealing mist is ineffective in water or in areas with other factors affecting the spread of the mist, as determined by the GM. It remains in the area for 1 minute or until any significant wind disperses it, whichever comes first.

>
[Revenant Blade](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3857)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Void" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=510" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 130

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Sickle](/Weapons.aspx?ID=364)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The mortal agents of powerful necromancers are a varied lot, but they tend to share two things in common: a deep and abiding fear of death, and a desperate hope that loyalty to their foul masters might be rewarded with some means of transcending it. To most of these wretched souls, this simple _[+1 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [sickle](/Weapons.aspx?ID=364)_ is as close as they will ever come to realizing that desire.

_Revenant blades_ are usually created in large numbers to arm a necromancer’s mortal troops before sending them into battle, and despite their name, they can be crafted from whichever base weapon is best suited for the expected conflict. Whatever form it takes, every revenant blade is adorned in some way with a small gem of deep black onyx. When you invest in the weapon, a small portion of your soul is transferred into the gem, bonding it to you and granting the weapon the effects of the decaying rune for as long as it remains invested.

Should you die in battle while invested in a _revenant blade_, its gem shatters, and your corpse rises 1 round later to continue the fight. You become an [undead](/MonsterTemplates.aspx?ID=3) creature under the GM’s control, although you generally retain the motivations and loyalties you had in life. The GM chooses what type of undead you become, selecting an appropriate undead creature that has a level no greater than your level – 5, to a minimum of 0. You can’t be raised from the dead by any means short of a [_wish_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=125) ritual until your undead form is destroyed.

</column>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 94

**Usage** affixed to a shield

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You use the affixed shield to [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) a melee attack

**Requirement** You're a master in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3), and you have the affixed shield [raised](/Actions.aspx?ID=98).
</row>

</column>

---

This heavy metal emblem is mounted on the face of the affixed shield and has a dull gray gemstone embedded at its center. When you Activate the talisman, the gem shatters, releasing a powerful shockwave in a 15-foot cone that must include the enemy who struck the triggering blow, if possible. Each creature in the cone takes 2d6 sonic damage with a DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. Any creature that fails its save is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 5 feet away from you (or 10 feet on a critical failure).

This arrow is made of polished animal horn, with the head of a rhinoceros carved in place of a traditional arrowhead. When an activated _rhino shot_ is fired, the ethereal form of a large rhinoceros takes shape around the projectile. On a successful Strike, the attack deals an additional 2d6 force damage, and the target must succeed at a DC 19 Fortitude save or be knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). If the hit with the _rhino shot_ was a critical success, the target is knocked prone unless it critically succeeds at its save.

fields.text: Item 5 Rhino Shot Uncommon Conjuration Consumable Magical Source Grand Bazaar pg. 30 Price 22 gp Ammunition any Activate Single Action Interact This arrow is made of polished animal horn, with the head of a rhinoceros carved in place of a traditional arrowhead. When an activated rhino shot is fired, the ethereal form of a large rhinoceros takes shape around the projectile. On a successful Strike, the attack deals an additional 2d6 force damage, and the target must succeed at a DC 19 Fortitude save or be knocked prone. If the hit with the rhino shot was a critical success, the target is knocked prone unless it critically succeeds at its save.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rhyton of the Radiant Ifrit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2607)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 124

**Price** 4,200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This exquisite, shimmering rhyton is made from volcanic glass and encrusted with rubies, garnets, and other red gemstones, with a blown glass sculpture of a snakelike fire elemental at its base. It was sculpted as part of a 10-piece set of drinking horns, created to match a powerful ifrit shuyookh's entertaining dinnerware, but it became separated from the rest of the collection. Whether for good or ill, the beautiful glass rhyton still carries tidings from its previous shuyookh owner, and you become their esteemed guest from afar whenever you hold it.

 The drinking horn functions as a [bottomless stein](/Equipment.aspx?ID=563), refilling with a common ale each time it's emptied. However, anyone holding the rhyton who whispers the name of its former shuyookh owner has the horn filled with their favorite wine, spirit, juice, or other beverage from anywhere across the many planes, as if their wish were granted by a magnanimous genie.

**Activate—Toast!** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))    **Effect** You raise a toast to a creature or creatures you're about to socialize with. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks against those creatures for 1 hour.

**Activate—Ifrit's Command** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** An ifrit's hospitality always comes with an implied threat. You cause the shuyookh to briefly appear and take its vengeance on those who would hurt you, the genie's “guest.” The shuyookh issues a 6th-rank [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=45) that targets all creatures [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23) to you in range instead of the usual number of targets. The shuyookh issues the same command to all of them. Each target that fails its save also feels all nourishment leached from it, becoming [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) as long as it's affected by the _command_.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Ridill](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1473)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 29

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 4
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=24)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This 12-foot sword was made by a [cyclops](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=25) in the ancient past. It might be the greatest dragon-killing weapon ever made, and [Fafnheir](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1725) justly fears it, which is why he keeps it hidden in his hoard. Runes of dragon slaying are written down its blade. _Ridill_ is a _+3 [major striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [dragon bane](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1041) [speed](/Equipment.aspx?ID=304) [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374) [greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=24)_. While wielding _Ridill_, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against [_fear_](/Spells.aspx?ID=110). This increases to +4 if the effect is from a [dragon](/Traits.aspx?ID=50). If you have an ability that depends on Large weapons (such as [barbarian giant instinct](/Instincts.aspx?ID=4)), it works with _Ridill_.

 _Ridill_ is always considered to have the appropriate material or damage type necessary to deactivate a dragon's [regeneration](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=26) or cause the dragon's weakness to apply. For example, _Ridill_ is considered to be [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=375) when attacking a [linnorm](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=69), while it would be treated as having dealt cold damage when attacking a [red dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=168). If the dragon has more than one weakness, only the highest value applies.

**Destruction** If you boil _Ridill_ in the blood of 10 different types of dragon ([blue dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=166) dragon, red dragon, etc.) and drop the eye of a cyclops seer into the brew, _Ridill_ melts away into nothingness.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    right="Item 8"
    pfs=""
>
[Right of Retribution](/Equipment.aspx?ID=933)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Abomination Vaults</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Contract" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=329" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #164: Hands of the Devil](/Sources.aspx?ID=75) pg. 75

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Profane powers of vengeance are yours to inflict. 

**Benefit** When a creature deals damage to you, you can call out for retribution as a reaction. Until the end of your next turn, you gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls against that creature. 

**Payment** If you wound a creature, it is your duty to kill it. If a creature survives for 24 hours after you deal it damage, you are [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9). If you already have the doomed condition, it increases by 1. 

**Hidden Condition** No more than once per year, the erinys can compel you to attack a creature of the erinys's choice that you can see. You are [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6) by the erinys and must fight the chosen creature for 1 minute. 

**Termination Clause** The contract demands that you enact bloody vengeance against anyone who has ever wronged you, but the nature of the vengeance is vague. You can end the contract by creating effigies of everyone you believe has ever wronged you, bleeding upon them all at once (at least 1 Hit Point per effigy), and destroying them.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

If you already have the doomed condition, it increases by 1. Hidden Condition No more than once per year, the erinys can compel you to attack a creature of the erinys's choice that you can see. You are controlled by the erinys and must fight the chosen creature for 1 minute. Termination Clause The contract demands that you enact bloody vengeance against anyone who has ever wronged you, but the nature of the vengeance is vague. You can end the contract by creating effigies of everyone you believe has ever wronged you, bleeding upon them all at once (at least 1 Hit Point per effigy), and destroying them.

    level="1"

>
[Righteous Fury](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3858)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Holy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=517" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 130

**Price** 6,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This gold-plated _[+2 greater striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [holy ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2842) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_ sports an ornate hilt bearing the religious symbol of [Ragathiel](/Deities.aspx?ID=481), General of Vengeance, and is painstakingly crafted to resemble the divine armaments wielded by the empyreal lord’s celestial soldiers in their battles against the forces of darkness. These weapons are popular among the ranks of those who hold the line against similar enemies, such as the Knights of Lastwall and warriors of the former Mendevian Crusade. 

**Activate—Great Vengeance** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737), [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** Your last action was a successful melee Strike with _righteous fury_ against a creature with the [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) trait;  **Effect** The sword emits a 20-foot-radius [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) of holy fire centered on your target, inflicting 2d8 spirit damage and 2d8 vitality damage to all enemies in the area (DC 34 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). Creatures that fail the save are [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round, and those that critically fail are blinded for 1 minute.

</column>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

---

Magical reagents slosh inside this rime-frosted pottery jar the size of a human head. Despite appearing to be rimed in hoarfrost, the jar is warm to the touch. Ilverani wizards create _rime jars_ to sustain themselves during the coldest winter nights.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** The jar draws off the cold and warms your body. If you have the [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) condition caused by exposure to [environmental cold](/Rules.aspx?ID=642), it removes the condition. For 8 hours after applying the rime, you treat extreme cold as severe cold.

>
[Ring of Bestial Friendship](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1749)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 588

**Price** 600 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The ring is made from a lock of green hair woven around several small gemstones. The ring of bestial friendship was created by Nyrissa for a specific reason: to allow her pawn Eirikk to manipulate the beasts of the Stolen Lands so as to sow discord among the PCs' nascent kingdom. As long as someone wears it, she can use spells like [_discern location_](/Spells.aspx?ID=75) and [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=268) on that person as if she possessed a part of their body. This effect does not work in reverse, despite being crafted from a lock of Nyrissa's hair. Instead, any attempt to use the ring as a body part to aid in casting a spell causes the ring instead to explode into a blast of lightning that causes 6d6 electricity damage to all creatures within 20 feet (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). This destroys the ring and automatically [counteracts](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the spell effect that triggered the explosion.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34) (heightened to 4th level) on an [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) or [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=20) within 30 feet. If the spell succeeds, it forms a mental bond between you and the target for the duration of the charm, which allows you to remain aware of the creature's present state, its direction from you, it's distance from you, and any conditions affecting it, as long as you are both on the same plane of existence and are both alive. If you fail to affect the creature with this charm, or once the charm ends (such as if it is [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371), or its duration expires), the creature becomes enraged and is immune to the ring's charm from that point on. The creature's rage drives it to attack you and grants it a +1 item bonus on all checks and DCs to do so for 1 hour.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Ring of Counterspells](/Equipment.aspx?ID=454)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 614

**Price** 925 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ornate silver ring bears two competing geometric designs of brightly colored and wildly clashing inlaid gemstones. A spellcaster can cast a single spell into this ring as long as no spell is currently stored within, expending the normal time, costs, and so forth to Cast the Spell. The spell’s effect doesn’t occur; the spell’s power is instead stored within the ring.

 When you invest a _ring of counterspells_, you immediately know the name and level of the spell stored inside, if any. A _ring of counterspells_ found as treasure has a 50% chance of having a spell stored in it. The GM determines that spell.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;   **Trigger** You are targeted by or within the area of the spell stored within the ring;  **Effect** You can attempt to counteract the triggering spell, using the level of the spell stored in the ring and a counteract modifier of +19. Once you do, the stored spell’s energy is spent, and the ring is empty.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;     **Effect** You harmlessly expend the stored spell, having no effect but emptying the ring so that another spell can be cast into it.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=163" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 154, [Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace](/Sources.aspx?ID=45) pg. 80

**Price** 15 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _ring of discretion_ magically conceals any armor and sheathed weapons you're wearing by either turning them [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) or creating the illusion of ordinary clothes. The ring doesn't change your appearance beyond concealing weapons and armor. As soon as you wield a weapon affected by the ring, the weapon becomes obvious to onlookers and is no longer affected until you sheathe the weapon for at least 1 minute. A creature can use the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) action to examine you and [disbelieve](/Rules.aspx?ID=267) this illusion (DC 15), and it can attempt to do so without using an action each time it hits you with an attack.

</column>

---

While the Kalistocrats of Druma profiteer off selling weapons to both Hellbreakers and Hellknights, they also offer options suitable for intelligence and counterintelligence efforts. This white gold ring grants you a +1 item bonus to skill checks to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363) that's primarily numerical or mathematical in nature as well as to skill checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) and [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394) to convince others of the fairness or accuracy of your judgments.

**Activate—Fair Assessment** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The Prophecies of Kalistrade reveal the secrets of wealth to you; this appears as a balance sheet of numbers only you can see. Choose an area of up to 1 cubic foot within 30 feet; you can estimate the value in gold pieces of any items within this area. If you attempt to estimate the value of items worn or held by a creature, you must succeed at a Society check to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363) against their Will DC.

[Ring of Maniacal Devices](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3437)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 310

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This magic ring seems like simple tarnished brass, but it enhances your curiosity about traps and devices of all kinds. You can use an Interact action to pull a [thieves' toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2758) from the ring. This toolkit appears in your hand and any part of it folds back into the ring if they would leave your possession. They grant you a +2 item bonus to Thievery checks to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=2411) and to [Pick a Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=2412), and the ring's insights grant you the same bonus to Crafting checks to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=2385) and [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=2384) snares and traps.

**Activate—Fireball Trap** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You create the effects of a [_rune trap_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=124) ritual containing [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1530). You can have only one trapped rune from a ring of maniacal devices active at a time, even if you have multiple rings, and the rune disappears if you lose your investiture in the ring.

</column>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This simple gold ring is engraved with eyes and is inlaid with a single amber-colored cat-eye gemstone. While the gemstone itself isn't magical, it gives off the eerie impression that it's watching you. A Firebrand makes use of this ring to determine if they've drawn the attention of locals and guards without the owner giving away the fact that they know others are watching. More powerful versions of the ring help Firebrands escape the sight of others when necessary.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The watchful eye of the cat-eye gemstone remains unmoving but feels as if it's surveying your surroundings. The eye continues this uncanny surveying for 1 minute. During this time, you can use a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, to focus on the ring. When you focus on the ring, it grows warm to the touch if you're being intentionally observed by creatures within 30 feet. The ring can only notice creatures that aren't [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) from you and that are intentionally watching you. The ring ignores people who are part of a crowd but aren't actively paying attention to you, for example.

fields.text: Item 3+ Ring of Observation Uncommon Divination Invested Magical Source Firebrands pg. 87 Usage worn Access Second-mark members of the Firebrands have access to this item. This simple gold ring is engraved with eyes and is inlaid with a single amber-colored cat-eye gemstone. While the gemstone itself isn't magical, it gives off the eerie impression that it's watching you. A Firebrand makes use of this ring to determine if they've drawn the attention of locals and guards without the owner giving away the fact that they know others are watching. More powerful versions of the ring help Firebrands escape the sight of others when necessary. Activate Single Action envision; Frequency once per day; Effect The watchful eye of the cat-eye gemstone remains unmoving but feels as if it's surveying your surroundings. The eye continues this uncanny surveying for 1 minute. During this time, you can use a single action, which has the concentrate trait, to focus on the ring. When you focus on the ring, it grows warm to the touch if you're being intentionally observed by creatures within 30 feet. The ring can only notice creatures that aren't hidden from you and that are intentionally watching you. The ring ignores people who are part of a crowd but aren't actively paying attention to you, for example. This band of interwoven gold and copper, traced with [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13) symbols, is topped with a gleaming, luminescent opal gently bleeding wisps of shadowstuff.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> command;     **Effect** You attempt to make the ring cast an arcane [_wish_](/Spells.aspx?ID=377) spell. However, if the ring doesn't deem the wish to be sufficiently selfless, the wish isn't cast and the ring can't be activated for 24 hours. You are [drained 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), whether or not the ring refuses the wish. Once the wish is cast, the _Ring of Recalcitrant Wishes_ has no powers, though it is rumored that the wearer's death in an act of profound self-sacrifice restores the _wish_ to the ring.

[Ring of Sneering Charity](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1645)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 161

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn ring

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This gold ring seems to offer good fortune to the wearer when they are charitable to those in need, but its curse was created to tear societies apart by inflaming class resentments and discrediting good works of true charity.

 Upon donning the ring, you must attempt a secret DC 25 Will save to avoid activating its magic. If you succeed, the ring's curse remains dormant, and it appears to be an exhausted item with no magic left. If you fail, the curse awakens, and the ring fuses to you.

 You are compelled to spend 10% of your wealth—and 10% of any future wealth you obtain—on charity. However, your acts of charity are insensitive and so insulting that they earn the recipients' enmity. For example, upon learning someone lost a child, you might toss money at them “to buy a new one.” You can't understand why your gifts aren't met with gratitude and resent the unappreciative recipients, and you firmly believe you should be able to call upon them for favors. You consider yourself an ideal philanthropist, and you constantly try to ingratiate yourself with other charitable organizations and individuals by offering to guide their donations to be more like your own.

</column>
