---

This simple iron ring is faceted with a bulbous geode lined with bright purple crystals. A _ring of stoneshifting_ grants you the ability to ignore difficult terrain caused by rubble or uneven ground made of stone and earth.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute;  **Frequency** three times per day;  **Requirements** You are standing on at least 5 feet of earthen material (such as stone, soil, clay, or sand); **Effect** You sink into the ground and emerge at another location within 100 miles. This location must have an earthen surface at least 5 feet deep and you must be able to identify the location precisely by both its position relative to your starting position and its appearance or other identifying features. You can’t carry [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) spaces with you to the destination, and if you attempt to do so, the activation fails.

This polished wooden ring constantly refreshes your body and mind. You don't need to eat or drink while wearing it, and you need only 2 hours of sleep per day to gain the benefits of 8 hours of sleep. A _ring of sustenance_ doesn't function until it's been worn and invested continuously for a week. Removing it resets this interval.

---

This ring, carved from green wood, bears carvings of tigers chasing each other through grasslands and forests. _Rings of the tiger_ are traditionally crafted by Kellids in northeastern Avistan, and are often worn by scouts or explorers. Many barbarians in these regions react poorly to anyone obviously not part of their people who dare to wear such a ring, but ironically have been known to gift these rings to outsiders who have proven their worth—potentially setting up a further clash in the future should that character encounter another group of Kellids who aren't familiar with how the wearer earned the right to wear the ring. A ring of the tiger grants a +1 item bonus on [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks and Perception checks made in outdoor wilderness areas, and it can be activated to momentarily transform the wearer's hand into a tiger's claw.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;    **Requirements** You aren't carrying anything in the hand on which the ring is worn; **Effect** Your hand becomes a tiger's claw, granting you an [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) claw [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that inflicts 1d6 slashing damage, and you Strike with the claw. Then the claw turns back to normal.

This simple golden ring has a large, red gemstone set into it that sparkles with an inner fire.

This is especially effective assistance against persistent fire damage, so you gain an immediate flat check to remove the persistent fire damage, and the DC typically decreases from 15 to 10.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />

This ring appears to be a [_ring of lies_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=456), but when invested, close investigation reveals angelic wings and divine creatures hidden on the face of the ring. When you invest the ring, you are rendered unable to tell a deliberate lie, in either speech or writing. If you attempt to omit the truth or phrase things truthfully but deceptively, roll a DC 11 flat check; on a failure, the ring itself blurts out the entire truth (as you believe it) as an answer. Keeping silent does not activate the ring’s curse. Once the curse has activated for the first time, the ring fuses to you.

>
[Ring of Wizardry](/Equipment.aspx?ID=462)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 615

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ring is made from the purest platinum and is covered in esoteric arcane symbols. It does nothing unless you have a spellcasting class feature with the arcane tradition. While wearing the _ring of wizardry_, you gain a +1 item bonus to Arcana checks and have two additional 1st-level arcane spell slots each day. You prepare spells in these slots or cast from them spontaneously, just as you normally cast your spells.

 If you take off the ring for any reason, you lose the additional spell slots. You can’t gain spell slots from more than one _ring of wizardry_ per day, nor can a single _ring of wizardry_ grant spell slots more than once per day.

 If you can cast arcane spells in a variety of different ways (such as if you are a [draconic bloodline sorcerer](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=5) with the [wizard multiclass archetype](/Feats.aspx?ID=742)), you can divide the spell slots as you wish among your various sources of arcane spells.

**Craft Requirements** You have a spellcasting class feature with the arcane tradition.

fields.text: Item 7+ Ring of Wizardry Uncommon Arcane Divination Invested Source Core Rulebook pg. 615 Usage worn This ring is made from the purest platinum and is covered in esoteric arcane symbols. It does nothing unless you have a spellcasting class feature with the arcane tradition. While wearing the ring of wizardry , you gain a +1 item bonus to Arcana checks and have two additional 1st-level arcane spell slots each day. You prepare spells in these slots or cast from them spontaneously, just as you normally cast your spells. If you take off the ring for any reason, you lose the additional spell slots. You can’t gain spell slots from more than one ring of wizardry per day, nor can a single ring of wizardry grant spell slots more than once per day. If you can cast arcane spells in a variety of different ways (such as if you are a draconic bloodline sorcerer with the wizard multiclass archetype), you can divide the spell slots as you wish among your various sources of arcane spells. Craft Requirements You have a spellcasting class feature with the arcane tradition. **Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 203 **Price** 14,000 gp **Usage** worn garment **Bulk** L **Base Armor** [Explorer's Clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=39) --- This soft, buttery smooth robe is _[+2 greater resilient ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [explorer’s clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=39)_ made from silk and [unicorn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3223) hair. The back and shoulders are appliquéd with clusters of angel feathers to form a motif of unfurled wings. On this robe are subtle arabesques, loops, and curlicues that are pleasing to the eye and evoke a sense of calm. When you wear this robe, you gain an [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) aura of purity and kindness that extends from you in a 30-foot emanation, granting you a +3 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) and to make [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) of creatures who are within your aura. **Activate—Compelled Nonviolence** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), incapacitation, [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** The wings of this robe extend, and your aura glows golden, briefly becoming visible as it does. Creatures within your aura who are [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=80), [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=82), or [unfriendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=97) to you must attempt a DC 36 Will saving throw with the following effects. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1.
**Failure** The creature is stunned 2.
**Critical Failure** As failure, and the creature can’t use any [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=2251) against you for 1 round.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 17"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Robe of Eyes](/Equipment.aspx?ID=463)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 615

**Price** 13,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn garment

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This garment appears to be an ordinary robe until donned, at which point numerous strange and alien eyes of varied shapes and colors open and blink across its fabric. While wearing the robe, you gain a +3 item bonus to Perception checks, and you constantly benefit from the effects of a 2nd-level [_see invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=271) spell.

 You can also see powerful magic auras. The highest-level magic aura within 30 feet of you glows in a color that reveals its school to you and allows you to determine where the effect originates. This can narrow down the origin point of the effect to a 5-foot-cube, but not more precisely than that.

 The _robe of eyes_ is not without its dangers. If any spell with the light trait is cast on you or your square while you are wearing the robe, you are blinded for a number of rounds equal to the spell’s level unless you succeed at a Fortitude save against the spell’s DC.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You pluck an eye from the robe and toss it into the air, where it turns invisible and floats to a destination you choose, with the same effect as a 5th-level [_prying eye_](/Spells.aspx?ID=239) spell. You can Sustain the Activation just as you would be able to Sustain the Spell. 

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 17 Robe of Eyes Uncommon Divination Invested Magical Source Core Rulebook pg. 615 Price 13,000 gp Usage worn garment Bulk 1 This garment appears to be an ordinary robe until donned, at which point numerous strange and alien eyes of varied shapes and colors open and blink across its fabric. While wearing the robe, you gain a +3 item bonus to Perception checks, and you constantly benefit from the effects of a 2nd-level see invisibility spell. You can also see powerful magic auras. The highest-level magic aura within 30 feet of you glows in a color that reveals its school to you and allows you to determine where the effect originates. This can narrow down the origin point of the effect to a 5-foot-cube, but not more precisely than that. The robe of eyes is not without its dangers. If any spell with the light trait is cast on you or your square while you are wearing the robe, you are blinded for a number of rounds equal to the spell’s level unless you succeed at a Fortitude save against the spell’s DC. Activate Single Action Interact; Effect You pluck an eye from the robe and toss it into the air, where it turns invisible and floats to a destination you choose, with the same effect as a 5th-level prying eye spell. You can Sustain the Activation just as you would be able to Sustain the Spell.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 99

**Price** 1,400 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn garment

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A robe of stone, decorated with patterns reminiscent of gems and geodes, constantly sheds tiny amounts of dust. While wearing it, you gain [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) in a radius of 10 feet, and you can speak and read [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109). Also, you can eat earth (soil, sand), gems (crystals, glass), and metal instead of food to meet your daily nutrition requirements. You find eating these materials as pleasant as food—the more valuable, the more delicious.

**Activate—Become Stone** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The cloak casts [_elemental form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=98) on you, transforming you into an earth elemental. In addition to the spell's normal effects, you can [Burrow](/Actions.aspx?ID=93) through any earthen matter, including rock, moving at the spell's burrow Speed, leaving no tunnels or signs of your passing. Also, the range of the tremorsense you gain from the robe increases to 30 feet.

[Robe of the Archmagi](/Equipment.aspx?ID=464)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 616

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn garment

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Explorer's Clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=2)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Embroidered with fine silver thread in ornate arcane patterns, these robes come in one of three colors depending on their attuned alignment. Good robes are gold, neutral robes are light blue, and evil robes are red. An [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64) or [good](/Traits.aspx?ID=83) robe gains the appropriate trait. The robes benefit only characters who can cast [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11) spells and whose alignment on the good-evil axis matches that of the robe. If your alignment does not match that of the robe, or you are not an arcane spellcaster, you are instead [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) while wearing a _robe of the archmagi_. This condition can't be removed in any way until you remove the robe.

 The robes are _+2 [greater resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [explorer's clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=2)_, and they grant a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against arcane spells and resistance 5 to damage from arcane spells.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You attempt a saving throw against an arcane spell, but you haven’t rolled yet;  **Effect** You automatically succeed at your save against the triggering arcane spell.

**Craft Requirements** You are an arcane spellcaster.

These robes, the traditional raiment of the runelord of envy, function as _+3 greater resilient [antimagic](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2787) greater [energy-resistant](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2788) [explorer's clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=39)_. The energy resistance granted by these robes can be selected from acid, cold, electricity, or fire when you perform your daily preparations—without these preparations, the robes default to cold resistance. </title>

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** arrow

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Each of these arrows is made from an immense [roc](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3170)’s flight feather, most of whose vanes have been trimmed to expose the arrow’s shaft. When an activated _roc-shaft arrow_ hits a target, the arrow briefly grows a pair of avian wings and attempts to carry off the target. The target must succeed at a Fortitude save or be moved to a space you choose within an area determined by the arrow’s type; if the target critically fails, the arrow can move them an additional 10 feet. If this would move the target into a [hazardous space](/Rules.aspx?ID=2368), this effect gains the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Dwarf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=54" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Saggorak" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=269" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City](/Sources.aspx?ID=13) pg. 75

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto medium or heavy armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Rock-braced_ armor makes you as hard to move as a boulder. Whenever another creature attempts to forcibly move you from your space, you gain a +4 item bonus to your Fortitude DC against the check to move you. If the creature would not normally need to attempt a check to move you, then the creature must succeed at an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check against your Fortitude DC (including the +4 item bonus) or you are unmoved.

</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 262

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

This powerful magic rod is inimical to all magic.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You touch the rod to a magical effect or magic item and attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the effect or item. Regardless of the result, the _rod of cancellation_ can't be activated again for 2d6 hours. On a success, the effect or item is deactivated for the same amount of time, and its duration, if any, continues to expire during that time. If you choose, you can instead completely drain the _rod of cancellation's_ magic on a success in order to completely drain the magic from the effect or item. If you do, both become completely non-magical and their magic can't be recovered, even by the [_remake_](/Spells.aspx?ID=249) spell.

 The _rod of cancellation_ automatically fails to counteract most [artifacts](/Equipment.aspx?Category=45) and similarly powerful items, but it reacts explosively when activated against a [_sphere of annihilation_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=620) without a counteract check.

>
[Rod of Razors](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1751)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Tech" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=434" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 589

**Price** 1,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Halberd](/Weapons.aspx?ID=26)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ornate, polearm-like weapon appears to be a cross between a halberd and a strange scepter of alien design. The rod's blades are edged in adamantine, and its haft is surprisingly elastic and can be used to extend the item's reach in combat dynamically, as needed.

 A rod of razors gains the effects of a _+2 [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374) [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [halberd](/Weapons.aspx?ID=26)_, but these effects are high-tech in nature, not magical. You can't etch property runes onto a _rod of razors_. The rod of razors has a long-lasting internal power source that does not require recharging from batteries (unlike the mindrender baton—see page 586), but if the rod of razors becomes [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2), its power supply grows unreliable. In such a case, each time the rod of razors is activated, the user must also succeed at a DC 5 flat check. Failure indicates that the rod's power supply fails and causes the rod to explode. This destroys the rod and causes 10d6 piercing damage and 10d6 slashing damage to the rod's wielder (DC 36 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Additionally, if the rod is destroyed through other means, the rod's current wielder must make a successful DC 11 flat check to avoid having the rod explode in the same way. Stories of desperate people intentionally destroying a rod of razors as a last ditch attack have inadvertently given these Numearian weapons a poor reputation among certain circles in that nation, particularly with the Technic League, who regard those who fight with these weapons as fools.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Strike;  **Frequency** six times per day;   **Effect** You fire a razor-sharp flechette from the rod of razors. This is a ranged weapon attack that has a range of 100 feet, a reload of 0, and the [deadly d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174) and [volley 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=201) traits. The flechette inflicts 3d8 piercing damage on a hit, and belongs to the [dart](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=6) weapon group. The flechette is an [adamantine](/Rules.aspx?ID=374) weapon.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Root Boots](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3137)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 74

**Price** 360 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn boots

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The soles of these plain leather boots look like coils of flattened roots. The boots allow for full-foot flexibility despite their sturdy make and smell faintly of evergreen trees. While worn and invested, your footsteps sound like rustling leaves, granting you a +1 item bonus to Stealth checks in a forest or wooded area. 

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The small roots extending from the soles of these boots allow you to move freely and easily across wood. For 10 minutes, you gain a 20-foot climb Speed on trees and other wooden surfaces, and you don't need to use your hands to climb. 

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You're standing on earth, and something attempts to move you against your will;  **Effect** The roots extend from your boots to grip the ground, granting you a +4 item bonus to your Fortitude DC against effects that attempt to move you, such as Shove or Pull.

</column>

This silk rope measures 50 feet long and is capable of holding up to 3,000 pounds. If the rope is ever cut, only the longest remaining portion retains its magic.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You hold one end of the rope and point to a destination. The rope animates for 1 minute, moving 10 feet per round until it reaches the destination or runs out of length. The rope can move across any non-damaging horizontal or vertical surface, but it can't extend upward without a surface to support it. At any point while the rope is animated, you can use an Interact action to wiggle the rope, giving it one of the following commands: stop in place, fasten securely to the nearest available object, detach from an object, or knot or unknot itself.

[Rose of Loves Lost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1646)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Evil" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=64" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 161

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

No thorns are visible on this ruby-red crystal rose, which seems to grant a boon to a loved one, but it draws three beads of blood when first bestowed upon an unwitting recipient. [Hags](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=59) delight in using the rose's curse to ruin young lovers, but it can be found anywhere—even buried innocently in a treasure hoard.

 You activate the _rose of loves lost_ by giving it to someone toward whom you feel romantic attraction. This item functions only if you feel genuine attraction and desire, and it doesn't function if you know the item's curse. If the target accepts the gift, they must succeed at a DC 27 Will save with the effects of [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34), except the duration is unlimited. Every 24 hours, the victim attempts another Will save to break the spell. If they fail three consecutive Will saves, they become [doomed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=9), as the rose inflicts a lethal wasting disease upon the recipient. This value can't decrease while the curse continues. Instead, it worsens every 3 days the victim fails to break the rose's spell, until the victim either dies or shakes off the enchantment. A successful saving throw or [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250) ends the charm and enables the victim to begin decreasing their doomed value.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

_Rovagug's mud_ smells and tastes like wet, sour earth. For 1 hour after you drink it, you have a +2 item bonus to saving throws against [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93) effects. Also, you can use a single action to breathe out a 20-foot cone of bitter vapor that causes an earth-shaking rumble that can be heard for 100 feet. Creatures and objects in the area take 5d6 damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save), decreasing Hardness by 5. An object's Hardness remains lowered for 1d4 rounds, and you can't use this breath again for the same amount of time.

For 1 hour after you drink it, you have a +2 item bonus to saving throws against incapacitation effects. Also, you can use a single action to breathe out a 20-foot cone of bitter vapor that causes an earth-shaking rumble that can be heard for 100 feet. _Rovagug's mud_ smells and tastes like wet, sour earth. For 1 hour after you drink it, you have a +2 item bonus to saving throws against [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93) effects. Also, you can use a single action to breathe out a 20-foot cone of bitter vapor that causes an earth-shaking rumble that can be heard for 100 feet. Creatures and objects in the area take 5d6 damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save), decreasing Hardness by 5. An object's Hardness remains lowered for 1d4 rounds, and you can't use this breath again for the same amount of time.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rowan Rifle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1185)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 166

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

In a dense forest within Arcadia, [djezet](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1410) fell from the sky millennia ago, even before Earthfall. While this metal was poisonous to most of the plant life growing nearby, one stubborn rowan tree refused to die, its roots slowly absorbing djezet in small particles from the ground until the entire plant was suffused with it. [Fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69) bowyers discovered the remarkable plant and coaxed it into growing into a very particular shape, its branching trunks woven together into a tightly twisted and naturally rifled barrel.

 One of the legendary star guns, Arcadia's greatest treasures, the _Rowan Rifle_ is a _+2 [greater fearsome](/Equipment.aspx?ID=731) [speed](/Equipment.aspx?ID=304) [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280)_ advanced firearm with a [range of increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of 300 feet. It deals 1d8 fire damage and has the [backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=172), [concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=401), and [fatal d12](/Traits.aspx?ID=178) traits.

 As a star gun, the _Rowan Rifle_ runs on magic, and doesn't use ammunition or black powder. As a weapon forged to protect the fey peoples of Arcadia, the _Rowan Rifle's_ enchantments prevent it from ever causing harm to a creature with the fey trait; any attempt to shoot a fey with it results in an automatic misfire. This legendary star gun is as much a badge of office as a weapon, as it denotes dominion over all Briarbough. If the _Rowan Rifle's_ wielder is fey, or if they were specifically given the _Rowan Rifle_ by a fey creature who recognized them as a worthy champion, they can use the following activations.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** You will the _Rowan Rifle_ to change the energy it fires from the white-hot energy of summer that glows like a star to the shivering chill of winter, the crackling electricity of the storm, or even the sonic vibrations of a roar. The _Rowan Rifle's_ damage type changes from its current damage type to cold, electricity, fire, or sonic. On the next sunrise, the _Rowan Rifle_ returns to dealing fire damage.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** The _Rowan Rifle_ fires a 60-foot line of liquid djezet that wraps around all creatures in the affected area before hardening, which impedes them with metallic vines unless the affected creature succeeds at a DC 35 Reflex save. A creature who fails the save takes a –15-foot circumstance penalty to their Speeds, and a creature who critically fails is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24). A creature who succeeds at a DC 35 [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) check ends this effect. Otherwise, the djezet vines last for 10 minutes before crumbling away.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes;   **Effect** You hold aloft the _Rowan Rifle_ and step into a tree in Briarbough, and you tree stride to another tree in Briarbough.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 16 Rowan Rifle Unique Magical Primal Source Guns & Gears (Remastered) pg. 166 Usage held in 2 hands Bulk 2 In a dense forest within Arcadia, djezet fell from the sky millennia ago, even before Earthfall. While this metal was poisonous to most of the plant life growing nearby, one stubborn rowan tree refused to die, its roots slowly absorbing djezet in small particles from the ground until the entire plant was suffused with it. Fey bowyers discovered the remarkable plant and coaxed it into growing into a very particular shape, its branching trunks woven together into a tightly twisted and naturally rifled barrel. One of the legendary star guns, Arcadia's greatest treasures, the Rowan Rifle is a +2 greater fearsome speed greater striking advanced firearm with a range of increment of 300 feet. It deals 1d8 fire damage and has the backstabber, concussive, and fatal d12 traits. As a star gun, the Rowan Rifle runs on magic, and doesn't use ammunition or black powder. As a weapon forged to protect the fey peoples of Arcadia, the Rowan Rifle's enchantments prevent it from ever causing harm to a creature with the fey trait; any attempt to shoot a fey with it results in an automatic misfire. This legendary star gun is as much a badge of office as a weapon, as it denotes dominion over all Briarbough. If the Rowan Rifle's wielder is fey, or if they were specifically given the Rowan Rifle by a fey creature who recognized them as a worthy champion, they can use the following activations. Activate Single Action (concentrate) Effect You will the Rowan Rifle to change the energy it fires from the white-hot energy of summer that glows like a star to the shivering chill of winter, the crackling electricity of the storm, or even the sonic vibrations of a roar. The Rowan Rifle's damage type changes from its current damage type to cold, electricity, fire, or sonic. On the next sunrise, the Rowan Rifle returns to dealing fire damage. Activate Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Effect The Rowan Rifle fires a 60-foot line of liquid djezet that wraps around all creatures in the affected area before hardening, which impedes them with metallic vines unless the affected creature succeeds at a DC 35 Reflex save. A creature who fails the save takes a –15-foot circumstance penalty to their Speeds, and a creature who critically fails is immobilized. A creature who succeeds at a DC 35 Escape check ends this effect. Otherwise, the djezet vines last for 10 minutes before crumbling away. Activate 1 minute (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per 10 minutes; Effect You hold aloft the Rowan Rifle and step into a tree in Briarbough, and you tree stride to another tree in Briarbough.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rowan Rifle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4289)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 166

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

In a dense forest within Arcadia, djezet fell from the sky millennia ago, even before Earthfall. While this metal was poisonous to most of the plant life growing nearby, one stubborn rowan tree refused to die, its roots slowly absorbing djezet in small particles from the ground until the entire plant was suffused with it. [Fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=599) bowyers discovered the remarkable plant and coaxed it into growing into a very particular shape, its branching trunks woven together into a tightly twisted and naturally rifled barrel.

One of the legendary star guns, Arcadia’s greatest treasures, the _Rowan Rifle_ is a _[+2](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [greater fearsome ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2837) [speed ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2844) greater striking advanced firearm_ with a range of increment of 300 feet. It deals 1d8 fire damage and has the [backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=544), [concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=846), and [fatal d12](/Traits.aspx?ID=597) traits.

As a star gun, the Rowan Rifle runs on magic, and doesn’t use ammunition or black powder. As a weapon forged to protect the fey peoples of Arcadia, the _Rowan Rifle’s_ enchantments prevent it from ever causing harm to a creature with the fey trait; any attempt to shoot a fey with it results in an automatic misfire. This legendary star gun is as much a badge of office as a weapon, as it denotes dominion over all Briarbough. If the Rowan Rifle’s wielder is fey, or if they were specifically given the _Rowan Rifle_ by a fey creature who recognized them as a worthy champion, they can use the following activations.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;     **Effect** You will the _Rowan Rifle_ to change the energy it fires from the white-hot energy of summer that glows like a star to the shivering chill of winter, the crackling electricity of the storm, or even the sonic vibrations of a roar. The _Rowan Rifle’s_ damage type changes from its current damage type to [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697). On the next sunrise, the _Rowan Rifle_ returns to dealing fire damage.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** The _Rowan Rifle_ fires a 60-foot [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) of liquid djezet that wraps around all creatures in the affected area before hardening, which impedes them with metallic vines unless the affected creature succeeds at a DC 35 Reflex save. A creature who fails the save takes a –15-foot circumstance penalty to their Speeds, and a creature who critically fails is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81). A creature who succeeds at a DC 35 [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) check ends this effect. Otherwise, the djezet vines last for 10 minutes before crumbling away.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> command, envision, Interact (1 minute);  **Frequency** once per 10 minutes;   **Effect** You hold aloft the _Rowan Rifle_ and step into a tree in Briarbough, and you tree stride to another tree in Briarbough.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 0"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rubbing Set](/Equipment.aspx?ID=874)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 115

**Price** 1 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Hands** 2

**Bulk** 1
</row>

**Access** Member of the Pathfinder Society.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

By using a rubbing set, you can quickly make a copy of carvings or etchings you find during your explorations, making them easier to accurately reproduce. This kit consists of a roll of thin onion-skin paper in a waterproof leather case, several thick wax crayons, and a bar of sealing wax that can be melted and used to temporarily hold the paper in place while you take the rubbing. Using the kit consumes the materials and provides a +1 item bonus on checks to document or reproduce artwork or writing that has been carved, etched, or otherwise physically added to a surface.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 48

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The frayed threads from the rips and tears in _Hao Jin's Tapestry_ still contain traces of the Ruby Phoenix's magic. Hao Jin has collected most of these loose strings, but others occasionally find these potent silk strands in unexpected places. A ruby string can fulfill the cost requirement for an 8th-level [_create demiplane_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=31) ritual. When used in this way, the ruby string negates the need for secondary casters, and you get a success for all secondary checks. Alternatively, you can activate it to create a smaller demiplane without requiring the ritual.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 8 hours (envision, Interact);     **Effect** You spin the thread to form a demiplane with the effects of a successful 8th-level _create demiplane_, but the space is a single 10-foot cube.

</column>

This jagged glyph, one of the [Thassilonian runes of sin](/Rules.aspx?ID=1567), reacts to magic of a particular school (there's no rune for [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), as it was considered lesser within sin magic). When you Cast a Spell of the school matching the sin, you gain resistance 5 to damage from spells until the start of your next turn. This resistance is increased to 7 against spells of the matching school. This tattoo has the school trait matching the rune: [abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2) for envy, [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) for gluttony, [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157) for greed, [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) for lust, [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92) for pride, [conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33) for sloth, and [evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65) for wrath.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 23"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Runewell Of Lust](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5226)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #221: Into the Apocalypse Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=371) pg. 76

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Three Actions" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** By splashing the _runewell_’s water on yourself while you stand within it, you transport yourself back to a space of your choice within 30 feet of the _anima focus_, which is currently located in Sorshen’s atrium.</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The _Runewell of Lust_ is a potent artifact and was the first of its kind among the runelords. As with all runewells, the _Runewell of Lust_ is immobile and located within a demiplane that's inexorably linked to it, but the anima focus that allows access to the demiplane and the runewell can be transported to new locations through a series of complex Sorshen's Sinuousrites known only to Sorshen herself.

 Originally, the _Runewell of Lust_ could absorb soul fragments of those who served Sorshen upon their deaths, granting her an essentially limitless supply of magical power she could use to fund potent rituals or craft magical items, but she disabled this ability soon after she woke years ago and decided it was time for a change. The _Runewell of Lust_ appears as a hot spring filled with soothing 3-foot-deep waters.

**Activate—Exit the Eye** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** By splashing the runewell's water on yourself while you stand within it, you transport yourself back to a space of your choice within 30 feet of the _anima focus_, which is currently located in Sorshen's atrium. 

---

Once Runelord Belimarius is defeated, the _Runewell of Lust_ can once again be activated as follows. 

**Activate—Scrying** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** The _runewell_ casts a 10th-rank _scrying_ spell (DC 46) to your specifications and gives you the benefits of telepathy for communicating with the target and 10th-rank _truesight_ for anything you watch through it. 

**Activate—Inner Dominance** <actions string="" /> ;     **Effect** 1 hour (concentrate, manipulate, mental) You spend an hour bathing in the _runewell_, gaining resistance 20 to mental damage and immunity to being [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64). As long as you benefit from Inner Dominance, the number of items you can invest each day is reduced by 2. As long as you benefit from Inner Dominance, you don’t age. The _Runewell of Lust_ can maintain Inner Dominance on up to seven creatures at a time, including Sorshen (who doesn’t count against this limit). Inner Dominance lasts until it’s dispelled, until the creature bearing it is slain, or until Sorshen chooses to end the effect as an Interact action.

**Destruction** If Sorshen is slain, the waters within the _Runewell of Lust_ immediately become normal water, destroying the _runewell_ in the process. The Eye of Desire is destroyed as well. Creatures not native to the Eye of Desire are immediately transported to the vicinity of the _runewell_’s linked _anima focus_ and become stunned 3; any foreign objects within the Eye of Desire at the time are similarly ejected.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Rusting ammunition is made using a [ore louse's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2665) saliva and, when activated, deals damage to objects or creatures primarily made of metal. The target takes [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) for a duration determined by the type of ammunition used. A creature that drops to 0 Hit Points while taking this persistent damage crumbles into fine powder; its gear remains. The ammunition's type determines the maximum amount of an object that's destroyed.

**Craft Requirements** Supply the saliva of an ore louse.

---

This [_+1_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2785) [_leather lamellar_](/Armor.aspx?ID=29) _armor_ incorporates the plates of an [ore louse’s](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2665) hide, woven together with the creature’s own sinew into a functional set of armor. While wearing the _rusting carapace_, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws against any effect that would rust you or your items, such as the ore louse’s Strikes that have the rust ability or the [_rust cloud_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1377) spell.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Oxidizing liquid seeps from between the segments of the rusting hide onto a nearby metal creature, non-magical metal hazard, or non-magical metal item of up to 1 Bulk. A targeted creature or hazard gets a DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2247) Fortitude save; a targeted item automatically gets a critical failure if unattended, but a creature holding or wearing it can attempt a DC 24 basic Reflex save. The rust deals 8d6 damage to a creature or hazard, plus 2d6 [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) on a failed save; it deals 2d6 damage to an item, plus 1d6 persistent damage on a failed save.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the hide of a [ore louse](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2665).

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 113 **Price** 75 gp --- This snare emits puffs of oxidizing chemicals that rapidly degrade metal items; skymetals and most precious metals are immune. The chemicals affect a non-magical metal item of up to 1 Bulk that the triggering creature is holding or openly wearing (determined randomly if the creature is holding or wearing more than one). The triggering creature must attempt a DC 25 Reflex saving throw. The snare deals 2d6 damage to the item; this damage ignores the item's Hardness and might deal persistent damage on a failed Reflex save. The creature, or an adjacent creature, can attempt to scrape off the chemicals as an Interact action to prevent the persistent damage; doing so reduces the DC of the flat check to end persistent damage to 10 and grants an immediate flat check. Thin iron or steel items, such as weapons, typically have 20 HP and a Broken Threshold of 10, and thicker iron or steel items, such as most suits of armor, typically have 36 HP and a Broken Threshold of 18. Other materials' statistics can be found on [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=730) and the statistics for items made of [precious materials](/Equipment.aspx?Category=22) on their respective pages. **Critical Success** The object is unaffected.
**Success** The object takes full damage.
**Failure** The object takes full damage as well as 1d6 [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).
**Critical Failure** The object takes double damage as well as 2d6 persistent damage.

May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Each _Arudora memento_ is unique in appearance, but all seven are approximately the same size. Carried by each of the cursed family members, these mementos have within them the power to unlock entire portions of Bastardhall from the ghostly cursed state the castle traditionally exists in. Each of the seven mementos has the following activation, but the section of castle unlocked by each activation, as well as each memento’s specific benefit granted to the PCs, varies by type. **Activate—Return Memento** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You place the memento into the appropriate statue’s clutches in the fountain located in area
**B3** of Bastardhall. The statue briefly animates to claim the memento, which turns to stone and becomes thereafter a permanent part of the statue, effectively destroying the memento while granting a boon to the party that persists for the remainder of this Adventure Path. A section of Bastardhall solidifies from its ghostly form, unlocking its reaches for the PCs to explore. **Destruction** An _Arudora memento_ is destroyed when it’s activated with Return Memento, and the boon it grants upon this returning lasts until the very end of the Adventure Path. Alisendra's Fan **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this elegant crimson hand fan is Returned, the dungeon (detailed in Chapter 5) is unlocked. The souls trapped in Bastardhall appreciate the end of Alisendra’s dominion and now whisper hints of truths in the ears of those who seek knowledge. The DCs for all checks made to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) are reduced by 1 for the rest of the Adventure Path. Augsten's Cudgel **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this bloodstained wooden cudgel is Returned, the reception halls (detailed in Chapter 4) are unlocked. Sometimes, violence is the only answer, and swift action to combat is rewarded. For the rest of the Adventure Path, all PCs gain a +1 bonus to any initiative rolls; this special bonus combines with all other bonuses. Dazerien's Thumbscrew **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this gory bronze thumbscrew is Returned, the private halls (detailed in Chapter 6) are unlocked. Rest becomes more rewarding now that the sadist of the dungeon has been defeated. For the rest of the Adventure Path, when the PCs take their 8-hour period of rest, they recover an additional number of Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) times their level. Irrokcis's Medallion **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this eerie medallion is Returned, the towers (detailed in Chapter 9) are unlocked, and the spirits of those trapped in Bastardhall rise up to aid the PCs. All weapon Strikes made by PCs deal an additional 1 spirit damage for the rest of the Adventure Path. Jinnivere's Riding Crop **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this leather riding crop is Returned, the cellars (detailed in Chapter 3) are unlocked. Companions are now more hearty and full of life—PC companions (such as familiars, eidolons, and animal companions) gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws for the remainder of this Adventure Path. fields.text: Item 0+ Arudora Memento May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies Rare Artifact Occult Source Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies pg. 235 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 1 Each Arudora memento is unique in appearance, but all seven are approximately the same size. Carried by each of the cursed family members, these mementos have within them the power to unlock entire portions of Bastardhall from the ghostly cursed state the castle traditionally exists in. Each of the seven mementos has the following activation, but the section of castle unlocked by each activation, as well as each memento’s specific benefit granted to the PCs, varies by type. Activate—Return Memento Three Actions (manipulate) Effect You place the memento into the appropriate statue’s clutches in the fountain located in area B3 of Bastardhall. The statue briefly animates to claim the memento, which turns to stone and becomes thereafter a permanent part of the statue, effectively destroying the memento while granting a boon to the party that persists for the remainder of this Adventure Path. A section of Bastardhall solidifies from its ghostly form, unlocking its reaches for the PCs to explore. Destruction An Arudora memento is destroyed when it’s activated with Return Memento, and the boon it grants upon this returning lasts until the very end of the Adventure Path. Item 0 Alisendra's Fan Source Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies pg. 235 Bulk L When this elegant crimson hand fan is Returned, the dungeon (detailed in Chapter 5) is unlocked. The souls trapped in Bastardhall appreciate the end of Alisendra’s dominion and now whisper hints of truths in the ears of those who seek knowledge. The DCs for all checks made to Recall Knowledge are reduced by 1 for the rest of the Adventure Path. Item 0 Augsten's Cudgel Source Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies pg. 235 Bulk L When this bloodstained wooden cudgel is Returned, the reception halls (detailed in Chapter 4) are unlocked. Sometimes, violence is the only answer, and swift action to combat is rewarded. For the rest of the Adventure Path, all PCs gain a +1 bonus to any initiative rolls; this special bonus combines with all other bonuses. Item 0 Dazerien's Thumbscrew Source Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies pg. 235 Bulk L When this gory bronze thumbscrew is Returned, the private halls (detailed in Chapter 6) are unlocked. Rest becomes more rewarding now that the sadist of the dungeon has been defeated. For the rest of the Adventure Path, when the PCs take their 8-hour period of rest, they recover an additional number of Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) times their level. Item 0 Irrokcis's Medallion Source Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies pg. 235 Bulk L When this eerie medallion is Returned, the towers (detailed in Chapter 9) are unlocked, and the spirits of those trapped in Bastardhall rise up to aid the PCs. All weapon Strikes made by PCs deal an additional 1 spirit damage for the rest of the Adventure Path. Item 0 Jinnivere's Riding Crop Source Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies pg. 235 Bulk L When this leather riding crop is Returned, the cellars (detailed in Chapter 3) are unlocked. Companions are now more hearty and full of life—PC companions (such as familiars, eidolons, and animal companions) gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws for the remainder of this Adventure Path. <row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

---

The euphemistically named saboteur's friend looks, smells, and tastes like an appetizing chocolate square. You lace the chocolate with reagents that induce a strong laxative effect. Saboteur's friend is useful for incapacitating rather than dealing lasting harm. Unlike some poisons, saboteur's friend can have its sickened condition reduced (but changing to a higher or lower stage after a save applies any sickened condition listed for that stage, as normal).

 **Saving Throw** DC 20 Fortitude; **Onset** 10 minutes; **Maximum Duration** 1 hour; **Stage 1** [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) (10 minutes); **Stage 2** [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) and sickened 2 (10 minutes); **Stage 3** enfeebled 1, [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15), and sickened 3 (10 minutes)

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Curtain Call</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Holy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=517" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #206: Bring the House Down](/Sources.aspx?ID=247) pg. 82

**Price** 40,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Lightning crackles from the wings flanking this helm, which is emblazoned with images of valkyries in the service of benevolent deities. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks and gain [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 20. When you [invest](/Actions.aspx?ID=2799) in the helm, you either increase your Strength score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score. If you are [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521), you become [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 2 as long as you wear the helm.

**Activate—Path of the Pegasus** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _sacred valkyrie helm_ casts [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) to your specifications. When you start this activation, each creature you target with this spell mounts a conjured pegasus who then carries them through reality to arrive at the specified location; each affected creature experiences the 10-minute activation as a kaleidoscopic ride through strange worlds and realities atop a pegasus’s back.

**Activate—Storm's Arms** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The helm casts a 9th-rank [_weapon storm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1758) to your specifications. At your option, all damage caused by this spell is [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) damage—in this option, the duplicated weapons created by the spell appear to be made of lightning.

</column>

Activate—Storm's Arms Two Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Frequency once per day; Effect The helm casts a 9th-rank weapon storm to your specifications. fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 0+"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Safe House](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2472)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 94

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Safe houses are locations that are difficult to find and provide sanctuary for groups or individuals in need of a suitable hiding place to lie low. These locations may be utilized by spies seeking refuge from enemies, accused criminals running from unjust or corrupt law enforcement, or any number of others sheltering from a hostile, unsafe, or oppressive situation. Many Firebrands make use of a safe house or set one up themselves in the course of their journeys to keep their presence hidden from spies or to find refuge while fleeing from dangerous locations.

 The costs associated with each level is the amount of money required to commission and establish a safe house of that level. This includes renting, purchasing, or constructing the location, bribing any informants for their discretion, and securing routes to and from the safe house in case of emergency. The cost of access to a safe house increases with the level of security it provides. Any creature attempting to locate a safe house must spend at least 2 hours to attempt to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49) on the  location, the DC of which is determined by the safe house's level. The DC of the check required to locate a given safe house is reduced by 1 for each day that the safe house remains in use. For this reason, a particular location is typically used for a maximum of three days, so longer stays in an area require movement between multiple locations. Once the location of a safe house has been compromised, it can't be used as a safe house again until significant time has passed or significant changes have occurred to the location, as determined by the GM.

 The GM determines the location and availability of a safe house along with its level. Costs for a safe house may be inflated for secure locations deep within enemy territory. Safe houses with higher security provide increased bonuses against hostile attempts to Gather Information to locate their targets. Level 1 safe houses are the least secure, but they're more widely available and more affordable as they're typically short-term rental houses or nooks in abandoned warehouses. Level 2 safe houses might be a hidden hut erected in a remote location or a secret room aboard a ship. Level 3 safe houses, being protected by a magical veil, a protocol of timed access, or a ferocious guardian beast, are challenging to locate for all but the most skilled seekers.

Once the location of a safe house has been compromised, it can't be used as a safe house again until significant time has passed or significant changes have occurred to the location, as determined by the GM. The GM determines the location and availability of a safe house along with its level. Costs for a safe house may be inflated for secure locations deep within enemy territory. Safe houses with higher security provide increased bonuses against hostile attempts to Gather Information to locate their targets. Level 1 safe houses are the least secure, but they're more widely available and more affordable as they're typically short-term rental houses or nooks in abandoned warehouses. Level 2 safe houses might be a hidden hut erected in a remote location or a secret room aboard a ship. Level 3 safe houses, being protected by a magical veil, a protocol of timed access, or a ferocious guardian beast, are challenging to locate for all but the most skilled seekers. **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 189 **Price** 24,000 gp **Usage** worn belt **Bulk** 1 --- The thin, glittering strands of rope that comprise this thick belt appear to be spun gold. Strung along the front of the belt are a collection of four multicolored, perfectly spherical beads: jade, turquoise, quartz, and amethyst. While wearing the lash, you gain a +3 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13). When you invest the belt, you either increase your Wisdom score by 2 or to 18, whichever would give you a higher score. **Activate** command, Interact; **Effect** You touch one of the jewels affixed to the sage's lash and speak a command word. Depending on the jewel, a different effect is produced that affects you and all living creatures in a 30-foot emanation. After the effect occurs, all four jewels disappear from the lash, reappearing at the next dawn.
  • **Jade** ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89), [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128)) Speak “purity” to produce a wave of green light that ends any [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) condition and any [ongoing poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) affecting creatures in the emanation.
  • **Turquoise** Speak “clarity” to grant all affected a +2 status bonus to their next Will save for 1 minute.
  • **Quartz** ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89), [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128)) Speak “lenity” to have each creature regain 30 Hit Points.
  • **Amethyst** ([divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=100), [revelation](/Traits.aspx?ID=138)) Speak “verity” to emit a magical trail of light from the lash that reveals the location of each creature in the emanation. For 1 round, if they would be [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), they become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) instead, and if they would be [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) or [unnoticed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=41) by a creature, they're [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) instead. A creature can attempt a DC 43 [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check to avoid the lash's detection.

A _Sairazul blue potion_ is a rich navy blue in color. Subjects of the [Crystalline Queen](/Deities.aspx?ID=107) produced the potion to protect themselves from the radiation [Ayrzul](/Deities.aspx?ID=102) left behind. For the next 8 hours, your skin becomes navy blue, and you gain resistance 5 to poison damage and void damage. If you drop to 0 Hit Points due to poison or void damage, the Sairazul blue within your body reacts, healing you for 8d8 Hit Points. The resistances the potion grants then end.

>
[Sambuca](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1200)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 177

**Price** 120 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A sambuca is a long, covered troop bridge designed to help troops move from sea to land. Preparing it for use requires lashing together two [galleys](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=6) or other ships of similar size. The sambuca is then mounted across the ships on one end with its length suspended upward, and attached to pulleys fastened to the tops of the ships' masts. Once the ships are moved into position, the sambuca can be lowered to rest on a battlement or other surface, allowing troops to rush from the ships onto their intended destination.

 The sambuca has AC 17, Fort +11, Ref +5, Hardness 8, HP 32 (BT 16), and object immunities. It's covered on all sides to protect those who cross, granting them greater cover. The end of the sambuca can be lowered by teams operating the pulleys in concert. This requires three crew members on each ship, and they can lower the far end of the sambuca by 15 feet each round they work.

</column>

The head of this arrow or bolt is a pointed glass cylinder with a hollow core. Upon hitting a corporeal creature, _sampling ammunition_ captures a small portion of the target's skin, blood, and flesh. The sample falls to the ground below wherever the creature was hit. This sample is sealed and magically preserved inside its chamber, although it deteriorates normally once the cylinder is opened. _Sampling ammunition_ can't collect samples from creatures made entirely of metal, stone, or other hard substances.

These sturdy leather sandals feature straps that wrap up to the knees. Etched in the leather are intricate patterns of stags leaping through the forest. You gain a +5-foot item bonus to your land Speed and a +3 item bonus on [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks when attempting to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378). When you invest the sandals, you either increase your Strength modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Trigger** You attempt a High Jump or Long Jump but you didn't Stride at least 10 feet;  **Effect** You can attempt the jump normally. It doesn't automatically fail.

[Sandalwood Fan](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2645)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 202

**Price** 2,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ornate fan's carving depicts a particular tableau from the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25), often of the site where the fan was created. Fanning it through the air creates a sandalwood-scented breeze and a crackling of magic. A _sandalwood fan_ is a planar key for [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) and similar magic. The _sandalwood fan_ makes it more likely for you to arrive where you intended, appearing 1d6×25 miles from your intended destination instead of the usual error range. This distance is further reduced to 1d4×25 miles if your destination is the scenery depicted on the fan.

**Activate—Plant Speech** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _sandalwood fan_ casts [_speak with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=294) and translate for [Fey](/Languages.aspx?ID=10) and [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108) on you. In addition to conversing with nearby plants, you can also communicate with any living plants you've spoken with in the past using this fan. These plants must either be on the same plane as you or on the Plane of Wood.

**Activate—Cloud of Leaves** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You summon leaves that protect your allies and identify enemies. All allies and indifferent creatures within 30 feet of you gain [lesser cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) for 1 round, while enemies come under the effect of [_revealing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=107) for 1 minute.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sandcastle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2595)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=153" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 100

**Price** 1,250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L inactivated
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _sandcastle_ comes in a cylindrical, waterproof satchel that contains densely packed fine sand. The sand's color depends on where it was collected when the item was made. This sand can be shaped and magically activated to create a fortification made of hard-packed sand. It can survive most ordinary weather, but a _sandcastle_ has little resilience against water. It collapses if activated on water or if the structure is caught in a deluge or heavy rainfall. Each 10-foot-by-10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 10, and 40 Hit Points. It's immune to critical hits and precision damage, and it has weakness to water 15. If destroyed, a section of the _sandcastle_ becomes a pile of sand, or wet sand if it was destroyed by water. This sand is [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453), which lasts for the remaining duration of the activation. It's easy to make handholds and footholds in the sand walls, so the DC to [climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) the walls is 15.

**Activate—Shape the Castle** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You empty the satchel and shape the sand into a miniature castle. When finished, you utter “build” in [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109), and the _sandcastle_ swiftly builds into a full-size structure. The castle is shaped as you choose, up to 120 feet in any dimension. Its walls must be 10 feet thick, and each story must be at least 10 feet tall from floor to ceiling. The _sandcastle_ has only rudimentary furnishings with no moving parts—even a chair or door is too complicated, but block-like benches and platforms can be created. Typically, the castle has little more than staircases and windows.

 You can return the _sandcastle_ to its portable form by using one Interact action to fill the item's satchel with sand from the castle.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

On Tekritanin holidays, children reenacted legendary battles of deities by playing with magical tops. Though the paint on this wooden top has long since faded, its magical runes once gleamed yellow-gold and fiery orange, evoking the color of the sky during a sandstorm. To set the top in motion, wind a string around its bottom and upward along its body, and then throw it while gripping the string.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Ineteract;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You throw the _sandstorm top_ 10 feet away from you. For 1 minute, as it spins, the top generates a magical sandstorm in a 5-foot radius. Any creature that starts its turn in the area or moves into the area takes 4d6 slashing damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). Additionally, a creature within the sandstorm must hold its breath or begin [suffocating](/Rules.aspx?ID=468).

To set the top in motion, wind a string around its bottom and upward along its body, and then throw it while gripping the string. Activate Single Action Ineteract; Frequency once per day; Effect You throw the sandstorm top 10 feet away from you. For 1 minute, as it spins, the top generates a magical sandstorm in a 5-foot radius. Any creature that starts its turn in the area or moves into the area takes 4d6 slashing damage (DC 30 basic Reflex save). Additionally, a creature within the sandstorm must hold its breath or begin suffocating.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sanguine Ammunition](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4964)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [High Seas](/Sources.aspx?ID=351) pg. 64

**Price** 75 gp

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

**Access** You're a member of the Red Mantis Assassins

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This wickedly barbed ammunition looks dangerous to even touch. It dissolves into blood on impact, leaving no trace if the target has blood. The target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to saves against diseases and poisons for 1 round. 

You can also [Activate](/Actions.aspx?ID=100) _sanguine ammunition_ as part of [Casting a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734). The spell must be 3rd-rank or lower, must take 1 or 2 actions to cast, must have the [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) or [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) trait, and must target a creature other than the caster. Casting a Spell this way has no effect; instead, a creature hit by _sanguine ammunition_ activated this way is targeted by the spell in addition to the item’s normal effects. If the target isn’t a valid target for the spell, the spell is lost. 

The ammunition affects only the target hit. If the spell requires a spell attack, use the result of your ranged attack roll to determine the degree of success of the spell. If the spell requires a save, the target attempts the save against your spell DC.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Sanguine Mutagen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1964)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=59" />
<trait label="Mutagen" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=116" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 60

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

You gain greatly increased blood production, filtering out contagions and boosting your endurance but causing your body to bloat with blood.

 **Benefit** You gain an item bonus to Fortitude and Reflex saves. This bonus improves when you attempt a save against an effect that has the [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) trait, [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) trait, or would give you the [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) condition.

 **Drawback** Whenever you take piercing or slashing damage, you take 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

pfs="Standard"

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Price** 3 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

The bonus is +1 (or +2 against disease, poison, or fatigued), and the duration is 1 minute.

</title>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Price** 300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

The bonus is +3 (or +4 against disease, poison, or fatigued), and the duration is 1 hour. When you roll a success on a save against a disease, poison, or effect that would give you the fatigued condition, you get a critical success instead.

<traits>

</traits>

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

This clear crystal pendant contains a drop of blood from a sorcerer that expands and contracts as you cast spells. A _sanguine pendant_ is associated with a specific sorcerer bloodline, and only sorcerers with that bloodline can invest this item. This item gains the trait matching the tradition of that bloodline. The pendant grants a +2 item bonus to both of your bloodline skills.

**Activate—Blood's Call** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You gain 1 Focus Point, which you can spend only to cast a bloodline spell. If you don't spend this Focus Point by the end of this turn, it's lost.

**Craft Requirements** You're a sorcerer with the associated bloodline.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Rusthenge</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rusthenge](/Sources.aspx?ID=215) pg. 59

**Price** 7 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>command</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You attempt a saving throw against a [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) or [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126).

 
</row>

</column>

---

This pin includes a piece of gauze wrapped around a dried herbal poultice. When you activate the _sanitizing pin_, the poultice dissolves and bolsters your body's defense against poison or disease. You gain a +2 status bonus on your Fortitude save against the initial exposure to the affliction. If you roll a critical failure on the triggering attempt, you get a failure instead.

</column>

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Shield** [Buckler](/Shields.aspx?ID=1), [Tower Shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=4)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This surprisingly weighty, though well-balanced, wooden [buckler](/Shields.aspx?ID=1) is emblazoned with the image of a sapling. The sapling withers as the shield takes damage.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The buckler expands, with the sapling image growing into a mighty oak tree. The buckler becomes a [tower shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=4), gaining the corresponding AC bonus, Speed penalty, and ability to [Take Cover](/Actions.aspx?ID=90). It keeps the same Hit Points and Broken Threshold, but its Hardness and Bulk increase by 2 in this form. The shield remains in this form until you Activate it again to revert it to a buckler.
